text:
Lane Hutson was Evolving-Hockey's most valuable defenseman in the league last season, and through 16 games of this one he looks like he plans to argue for a repeat. Montreal takes 58.7% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on the ice and is 11.4 points better than when he sits. That gap is enormous.

He has 16 points, a four-game point streak built entirely on assists (six of them), and the same profile as always: carries the puck in on 54% of his entries per Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking, sets up nearly everything, shoots little. His 2.40 points per 60 sits right on his talent range.

The nits are worth naming. Evolving-Hockey noted his 2025-26 results ran ahead of his chances, his shooting is a little hot (10.3%), and his ice time has dipped about three minutes over his last ten. The Hockey News' Karine Hains counted four Hutson giveaways through two periods against Utah, though high-volume puck carriers rack those up. Still, he is 22, 5'9", and the engine of a team that keeps winning. Our projection lands near 77 points.
headline: Hutson's numbers say Montreal runs through him
